name: Una Troubridge
bio: Sculptor, translator and diarist, born Margot Elena Gertrude Taylor on 8 March 1887 and generally known as Una Vincenzo. She trained at the Royal College of Art, sculpted a bust of Nijinsky in his role as the faun (1912), and later became the principal English translator of Colette. She married the naval officer Sir Ernest Troubridge in 1908 and had a daughter, Andrea, in 1910; the Ransom Center's sketch records that the Troubridges "were separated by 1919 because of Una's relationship with Radclyffe Hall". She was Mabel Batten's cousin, met Hall in 1915, and was her partner until Hall's death in 1943, afterwards writing The Life and Death of Radclyffe Hall (1961). Her diaries run to 131 volumes at the Ransom Center. She does not appear in Wilde's Complete Letters. She died in Rome on 24 September 1963.
bio_note: Cook (2014, p. 108) names her with Hall among women who "seem to have been considered" for the Order of Chaeronea - a hedge too weak to carry an Ives edge.
